name: wingman
description: A set of photos in, a dating-app-ready lineup out. Every photo is measured — faces found by an ONNX detector (UltraFace), face size and position, whether it is a headshot, a half-body, a full-body, a wide shot or a group; sharpness as Laplacian variance, exposure and contrast off the histogram, near-duplicates by perceptual hash, GPS coordinates hiding in EXIF — and each issue costs points with a sentence saying why. The lineup picks the best N in the order they should go up: one sharp solo face leads, then variety (portrait, full-body, headshot, a wider shot), duplicates collapse to the sharper one, a group shot goes late and at most once, and `gaps` names what the set is missing that no edit adds. Render crops face-aware to Tinder, Hinge or Bumble's card ratio (eyes ~40% down, headroom kept), polishes gently (autocontrast, exposure lift on dark frames, a light sharpen) and writes a JPEG with every byte of metadata stripped. No skin smoothing, no background replacement, no reshaping; expression and outfit are not scored because nothing here can see them, and the audit says so. Nothing leaves the box. Twelve MCP tools, a REST API and the console on one port.

measures.faces: UltraFace RFB-320 on onnxruntime, letterboxed to 320x240, NMS 0.3, threshold 0.7; falls back to a YCbCr skin blob and says so
measures.role: headshot ≥ 28% of frame height, portrait ≥ 12%, full ≥ 4%, far below; group when a second face is ≥ half the first; scene when none
measures.sharpness: Laplacian variance on a 640-wide grey copy; under 25 blurry, under 60 soft; the face crop is measured separately
measures.exposure: mean luminance under 60 dark, over 200 bright; clipped pixels at both ends; std under 30 flat
measures.privacy: EXIF GPS flagged on intake; every render is written without exif, icc, xmp or thumbnail

lineup: lead = sharp solo face 15-45% of frame, no bad issues, score ≥ 60; then portrait, full, headshot, scene; group after slot 3 and at most one; anything under min_score (35) is left out with its top issue named

endpoints.sets: GET /sets (loopback or x-wingman-token) | POST /sets {name?} | GET /sets/:id | DELETE /sets/:id | POST /sets/:id/name
endpoints.photos: POST /photos multipart files[] + set= | JSON {set?, data|files|path|dir|url} | DELETE /photos/:set/:photo
endpoints.render: POST /render {set, photo?, preset?, ratio?, size?, zoom?, polish?, only_lineup?, n?}
endpoints.export: POST /export {set, preset?, n?, zoom?, polish?, quality?}

requires.Pillow: decoding, crop, resize, polish, JPEG out
requires.onnxruntime: the face detector (optional — a skin-colour fallback runs without it)
requires.pillow-heif: optional — HEIC straight from an iPhone

env.PORT: port for API, console and MCP (default 50830)
env.WINGMAN_BIND: bind address (default 0.0.0.0; 127.0.0.1 to keep it off the network entirely)

auth.reads: a set is addressed by a 16-hex unguessable id; GET /sets (the list) answers only loopback callers or x-wingman-token from ~/.mod/wingman/token
auth.writes: open on the same terms — this module holds personal photos, not keys or money; bind to 127.0.0.1 or put it behind the gateway's auth if it must be public
